notes: Printed conjecture 'a(n+15) == 0 (mod 30) for n > 4' is false: odd_of_three_le (A109926_mathlib.lean) shows every k with at least 3 primes k - 2^r is odd (even k: k - 2^r = 2 fixes r), so A109926_not_dvd_30: a(m) is never divisible by 30 for m >= 3; e.g. a(20) = 2282745465 = 15 (mod 30). Data a(5..20) are all 15 (mod 30), so the intended reading is a(n)+15 == 0 (mod 30). Its odd part is proved here; 3 | a(n) (Wilson's first conjecture) and 5 | a(n) for all n are famous-strength (need control of primes k - 2^r for all k < a(n); existence of a(n) for every n is itself unknown) and were not attempted. Axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Outside Lean: a(20) has exactly 20 representations (PARI, certificate/a20.gp); its minimality is the entry's.

sources.cite: P. Erdős, On integers of the form 2^k + p and some related problems, Summa Brasil. Math. 2 (1950)

prior_art.note: Misprint (a(n+15) for a(n)+15) not noted in the entry; mod 3 and mod 15 claims open and famous-strength.
